name: James Paul Pieczonka
evaluation: Judge Pieczonka was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1983; elected in 2014 and retained in 2020. He was initially assigned to the First Municipal Paternity, Traffic and Misdemeanor matters in Rolling Meadows. In 2015 he was assigned to the Civil Division; in 2019 to the Civil Jury Section. Judge Pieczonka currently presides over civil jury trials involving personal injury, property damage, torts, and contracts among other issues. He also serves in rotation with other judges for after-hours duty for emergency matters. Comments regarding Judge Pieczonka’s judicial performance were positive. He is described as well prepared, consistent, patient, professional, fair, diligent, and efficient.

name: John G. Mulroe
evaluation: Judge Mulroe was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1988. He started his career as a Cook County State’s Attorney. From 1995 until his appointment in 2019, he had his own firm, concentrating in real estate, probate, personal injury, and criminal defense. From 2010 to 2019, he also served as an Illinois state senator. After his appointment, Judge Mulroe was assigned to Traffic Court and also served in Forcible Entry/Detainer and Eviction Courts. After his election in 2020, he was transferred to Juvenile Justice, where he has been ever since. Judge Mulroe has volunteered as a mock trial judge and coach for community and legal organizations. He has worked with Redeploy Illinois, with the pilot program in his courtroom. He is also working on the bench book for Juvenile Justice Court. All comments about Judge Mulroe’s legal knowledge, sensitivity, temperament, diligence, and character were very favorable.

name: Maura McMahon Zeller
evaluation: Judge Zeller was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1993. She was elected to a circuit court countywide vacancy in 2020. She was assigned to Traffic Court until she her transfer to the Domestic Relations Division in October 2021, where she has served ever since. She handles an Individual Calendar, wherein she hears cases from filing to conclusion, and post-decree. Prior to becoming a judge, Judge Zeller worked as a Public Guardian, representing children in the Child Protection Division of Juvenile Court for 10 years. For 17 years thereafter, she had her own practice in guardianships; she served as a Child Representative and mediator in Domestic Relations. Interviewees described her legal knowledge, diligence, sensitivity, and character as good, with temperament being a particular strong point.

name: Michael A. Forti
evaluation: Judge Forti was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1980. After a career in private practice, employment with the City of Chicago – Law Department and Chief Counsel for the Illinois Department of Transportation, he was appointed to the circuit court in 2016, reappointed in 2018, became an associate judge in January 2020, then elected in November. His current assignment is in Domestic Relations where he presides over an Individual Calendar. He is a member of various bar and judicial associations and sits on the board of the Italian American Judges Association and Music of the Baroque. Attorneys described him as highly skilled and knowledgeable on domestic relations matters, issuing well-reasoned decisions, while being respectful and patient.

name: Caroline Kate Moreland
evaluation: Judge Moreland was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1995. She was appointed to the circuit court in 2010; reappointed in 2012; elected in 2014 and retained in 2020. She is currently assigned to the Chancery Division where she handles a broad variety of complex civil matters: administrative reviews, corporate and business disputes, trust litigation and insurance coverage. Judge Moreland is said to be prepared and knowledgeable about cases. She is fair to everyone, and considerate of pro se litigants. She manages her courtroom well and gives parties equal time to present their cases.

name: Kerry M. Kennedy
evaluation: Judge Kennedy was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1979. After a career as an assistant public defender, he was elected to the Circuit Court in 2002 and, subsequently, retained three times. In July 2021, he was named the Presiding Judge of the Fifth Municipal District (Bridgeview). Prior to this, since 2003 he spent time sitting in various courtrooms in the Fifth District. He is a member of various bar and judicial organizations, and in 2017 was named Jurist of the Year by the Southwest Suburban Bar Association. In addition to his administrative duties, he often presides over the various court calls in the district. Attorneys who have appeared before him praised his in-depth knowledge of various areas of the law and ability to be pragmatic. He is considered to be well-prepared with high integrity.

name: Thomas M. Cushing
evaluation: Judge Cushing was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1988. He was appointed to the circuit court in June 2019 and elected in 2020. Prior to his appointment, he had been “of counsel” to Christoper Kreid & Associates since 2010 where he focused on civil litigation. After prior assignments in Traffic and Domestic Violence, in 2023 he has been assigned to the Law Division – Jury at the First Municipal District (Daley Center). He has spoken as a panelist on legal issues and is a member of different bar associations. Attorneys praised his legal knowledge and ability, his diligence, integrity, and even keeled temperament.

name: Elizabeth Anne Walsh
evaluation: Judge Walsh was elected in 2020. She served in the Traffic Division until February 2021, when she was transferred to the First Municipal Non-Jury Division, where she served until February of 2025. She presided over a variety of cases from start to finish, including a large number of self-represented litigants. In February 2025, she was assigned to her current call, Law Motions, where her caseload included car accidents, dog bites, medical malpractice, and defamation, among other issues. Prior to her election, Judge Walsh worked for a firm handling defending insureds from State Farm from pleadings through trial. Those familiar with Judge Walsh’s conduct on the bench were uniformly positive about her legal knowledge, sensitivity, temperament, diligence, and character.

name: Sheree Desiree Henry
evaluation: Judge Henry was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1986. After a career as an assistant public defender she was appointed to the circuit court in August 2019 and elected to a countywide vacancy in 2020. Since October 2020 she has been assigned to the Fourth Municipal District (Maywood). She has been a speaker to new judges and is a member of various bar and judicial associations. She has been a board member of the Illinois Judicial Council and received their President’s Award in 2023 and the Distinguished Service Award in 2025. She is also a veteran of the Illinois Army National Guard. The investigation revealed overall feedback that she is a good judge who mainly follows the law and who is honest, respectful and calm.

name: Robert D. Kuzas
evaluation: Judge Kuzas was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1989. He was elected to the circuit court in 2014 and retained in 2020. He is assigned to First Municipal, presiding over preliminary hearings in Branch 44. Prior to his election, he was in private practice focusing on criminal defense. He is a member of various judicial associations and has served on the board for the Jesse White Tumbling Team. Attorneys described him as a knowledgeable judge who applies the law carefully, is professional and diligent.

name: Maureen Ward Kirby
evaluation: Judge Ward Kirby was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1989. She was appointed to the circuit court in 2007; elected in 2008; retained in 2014 and 2020. She has been assigned to the County Division in 2009, and in June 2025 was named Presiding Judge, after serving as acting Presiding Judge since 2023. Prior to her appointment she had been in private practice handling complex commercial litigation. She has frequently spoken on civil mental health issues and serves on Illinois Supreme Court Committees. She is a member of various bar and judicial organizations and has served on the Boards of the Illinois Judges Association and the Illinois Judges Foundation. She is highly regarded by attorneys for her legal knowledge, integrity, even-handedness and ability to handle a variety of legal issues.

name: Anthony C. Kyriakopoulos
evaluation: Judge Kyriakopoulos was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1990. After a career as a prosecutor, he was appointed to the circuit court in February 2010; reappointed in August 2012; elected in 2014 and retained in 2020. Since 2015 he has been assigned to the Chancery Division, Mortgage Foreclosure/Mechanics Lien Section. He received a service award from the Hellenic Bar Association in 2023, and is currently on their Board, as well as serving as president of the Order of Themis. He has been a speaker on legal topics and involved in other community activities. Attorneys reported that he is professional, good at explaining the law to pro se litigants, and treats all equally.

name: Sondra Nicole Denmark
evaluation: Judge Denmark was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2004; After a career as a prosecutor, she was appointed to the circuit court in December 2018 and elected in 2020. Prior to joining the bench, she had been an Assistant State’s Attorney in Will County for ten years. After an initial assignment in Traffic, she moved to First Municipal; in January 2026 she was appointed Supervising Judge of First Municipal Trial Section. She has been a speaker in legal topics, is a member of various bar and judicial associations, and participated in community activities. Attorneys gave positive feedback regarding her legal knowledge, her firm grasp of case law, and her ability to explain things to jurors and pro se litigants.

name: Celestia L. Mays
evaluation: Judge Mays was admitted to the Illinois bar in 1990; appointed to the circuit court in January 2019 and became an associate judge in January 2020. She was elected to a countywide vacancy in 2020 and is currently assigned to the 4th Municipal District (Maywood), hearing a variety of matters. Prior to her appointment she was a sole practitioner chaired committees for various bar and judicial groups and received the Cook County Bar Association Presidential Award in 2021, the Outstanding Service Award from the Illinois Judicial Council in 2025. She is considered by attorneys to be patient, respectful, and a good researcher, with good legal knowledge.

name: Daniel Edward Maloney
evaluation: Judge Maloney was admitted to the Illinois bar in 2001. He spent the majority of his career as an Assistant State’s Attorney in Cook County, where he was last assigned in the Narcotics Unit. Judge Maloney was appointed to the circuit court in 2019 and elected in 2020. His first short assignment was in Traffic Court. Since 2019, he has been assigned to the Sixth Municipal District (Markham) in the Traffic and Misdemeanor rooms. He has also served in the Problem Solving Courts there, which involve substance addiction, and mental health issues. Judge Maloney has been a speaker on the Problem Solving Courts at the Southwest Bar Association and the ISBA. He is active in church and community organizations as a coach and mock trial coach/judge. Comments about Judge Maloney’s legal knowledge, sensitivity, character, temperament, and diligence were all positive.
